title: P25-family depth-for-width at the 10M cap: five Peri-LN blocks of width 448 (8 heads of 56, D_FF 1280, 9.88M params) instead of six of width 384 on the 153-claude Lean incumbent
description: P25 (wider residual stream) via depth-for-width reallocation: N_LAYER 6 -> 5 and D 384 -> 448 (heads 48 -> 56 dims), D_FF held at 1280, 9,880,768 params (+3.4%), everything else identical to 153-claude. Width is the only lever that paid twice under the Lean protocol (151, 153: round-1 RL targets 432 -> 736) while every extra block or loop lost (102, 105, 125/126, 132, 134, 145, 166, 172), so a wider residual stream and larger heads should give expert iteration a better long-proof starting sampler than a sixth block does.
hypothesis: At fixed params the 7+ line sampler RL starts from is limited by per-position representational width (how many names/hypotheses the residual stream and each head can carry), not by depth: 6 blocks beat 5 only at width 256 (101, +16), and depth beyond 6 has lost every time. Trading one block for 17% more width (and 17% larger heads for the NoPE citation lookups) should raise round-1 targets solved and hence the metric, at equal or slightly higher steps since fewer, larger matmuls run faster (bench: 11.85 vs 11.53 steps/s over the first 60 s).
expected_delta: -40 to +35 theorems at >=7 (central +3); steps 4,300-5,000 per seed (bench 11.85 steps/s over the first 60 s vs 153's 11.53 which became 4,503 mean; expect ~4,630); epochs 3.8-4.4; final val loss 0.075-0.095; held-out greedy 0.95-0.98; round-1 RL targets solved at or above 153's mean 736 if the mechanism holds (falsifier: mean < 600 means the lost block matters more than width); round-4 RL-solved 1,120-1,220; RL sampling >= 200 samples/s in round 1 (bench 184 vs 148-fable's 186); totals 1,550-2,000 s

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, 153-claude incumbent code with N_LAYER 6 -> 5 and D 384 -> 448 (8 heads of 56, D_FF held at 1280); every other line of pretrain.py unchanged
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 and 0 for heads 5..8 (NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys. Head dim 56 (was 48)
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107), eps 1e-5 everywhere
arch.change: P25-family depth-for-width reallocation at the 10M cap: five Peri-LN blocks of width 448 instead of six of width 384. Per block: qkv (1344,448)+b, proj (448,448)+b, fc1 (1280,448)+b, fc2 (448,1280)+b, four LayerNorms = 1,956,800 params (153: 1,579,136); 5 blocks = 9,784,000; emb and head 107 x 448 each = 95,872; ln_f 896. MLP ratio 1280/448 = 2.86x (153: 3.33x). The MTP module follows D: one 448-wide Peri-LN block + (448,896) input proj + two LayerNorms
arch.n_params_detail: 9,880,768 handed off (bench_pretrain on an A40 reported 9,880,768), 119,232 under the cap; MTP module (pretraining only, dropped at handoff): 2,360,000 (153: 1,875,584)
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 5, 448, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks (d_ff 1280), load state
arch.kv_cache: unchanged code; 5 per-block caches instead of 6

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms; the MTP module's five 2D matrices (block qkv split into Q/K/V, block proj, fc1, fc2, and the (384,768) input proj) join Muon and its LayerNorms/biases join AdamW (unchanged from 151)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock, unchanged from 129/151: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 448 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (1280,448) and fc2 (448,1280) sqrt(1280/448) = 1.69, head (107,448) 1, MTP proj (448,896) sqrt(2); MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 5 x (qkv.weight (1344,448) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight, plus the MTP module's 5 matrices: 26 Muon matrices (153: 30)
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,448,448), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (1280,448) is not (3D, D) since 1280 != 1344, so it is orthogonalized whole
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1 on all 21 trunk+head Muon matrices (and the MTP module's); AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers (unchanged)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights (no rescale); the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW (lr 3e-4, wd 0.1) on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 20 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (448,896): 26 Muon matrices during pretraining; the handoff model's parameters are 9,880,768

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); mean padded tokens per step ~18.3k of which ~18.3k real (>99% fill), vs the incumbent's ~51-54k padded slots for ~17.3k real tokens
batch.change: fairseq-style max-tokens batching replaces fixed 128 random records per step: per epoch, randperm the training records (GPU generator, seed), stable-argsort by total length so equal lengths stay shuffled, cut greedily into consecutive runs with count * max_len <= 18,432, then shuffle the run order with random.Random(seed). Loss is the same per-token mean over the batch's proof tokens; the shift augmentation, Muon/AdamW updates, warmup, clip and wall-clock cosine are unchanged. The val slice still uses fixed chunks of 128.
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.init: unchanged rule from 148/151/153: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D block and MTP parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so element std stays 0.02 at width 448; LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0
